title: Modi and Macron Have Opened 'Bharat Innovates' in Nice. 120 Indian Startups Are Pitching to European Capital.
excerpt: The three-day conclave at the Palais des Expositions has brought together 500 investors, 15 top Indian universities, and a startup cohort that holds 1,500 patents and has raised over $1.5 billion collectively.
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and French President Emmanuel Macron jointly inaugurated the Bharat Innovates 2026 conclave in Nice on Sunday, launching what is now the largest Indian innovation showcase ever held in Europe.

The event, organised by India's Ministry of Education at the Palais des Expositions de Nice, has brought together 120 Indian deep-tech startups selected from over 3,000 applicants. The cohort collectively holds more than 1,500 patents and has raised over $1.5 billion in funding. It includes publicly listed companies like ideaForge and Ather Energy alongside early-stage ventures spanning 13 sectors — from advanced computing and semiconductors to biotechnology, space technology, and climate solutions.

## Macron Cites Chandrayaan, Modi Calls It a Bridge

Macron welcomed Modi with a hug and a handshake before the two leaders took the stage together. "It is a huge honour, dear Prime Minister Narendra Modi, to welcome you here in Nice," the French president said. He pointed to India's Chandrayaan-3 lunar landing as proof of the country's innovation capacity: "The feat of landing on the Moon's south pole was accomplished in record time, thereby demonstrating India's strength and innovative capability."

Modi, addressing a packed hall of innovators and venture capitalists, framed the event as something beyond a trade exercise. "There are few relations which are driven by shared vision, besides shared interests. India-France relations are one such tie," he said. "This platform of 'Bharat Innovates' is becoming a bridge between Indian talent and European capital — a platform where India's young minds are receiving the opportunity to connect with European expertise."

## The Ecosystem in the Room

More than 500 investors — including leading venture capital firms, corporate funds, and global CEOs — are attending the three-day conclave, which runs through June 16. Around 15 Indian higher education institutions, including IITs and IISc, are presenting research projects alongside the startup cohort.

Before the inauguration, Modi held private interactions with several business leaders, including OYO Rooms CEO Ritesh Agarwal and Indian entrepreneur Ronnie Screwvala.

Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, who released strategic documents profiling the selected startups ahead of the event, said Bharat Innovates had already generated nearly $20 million in investment commitments "either finalised or nearing closure." Principal Scientific Adviser Ajay Kumar Sood, who chaired the committee that selected the 120 startups, called the event "a reflection of India's immense potential on the world stage."

## The Bigger Picture

The conclave is part of the India-France Year of Innovation, following the elevation of the bilateral relationship to a "Special Global Strategic Partnership" in February 2026. Cooperation between New Delhi and Paris now spans defence, nuclear energy, space, AI, and digital technology.

For Modi, the Nice event is the first leg of a packed European schedule. He will travel to Slovakia later on Sunday for the first-ever state visit by an Indian prime minister to Bratislava, before returning to France for the G7 Summit in Evian on June 16-17 — where a closely watched bilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump is expected on June 17.

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal are also part of the delegation. Multiple MoUs between Indian startups, academic institutions, and global industry partners are expected to be signed over the three days.

The message from Nice is straightforward: India is no longer just exporting engineers. It is exporting companies.
